map.骨质疏松(FRAX)骨折风险评估器 使用指南: Osteoporosis (FRAX) fracture risk assessor user guide
map.基于FRAX模型评估10年主要骨质疏松性骨折和髋部骨折概率，辅助治疗决策: Estimates the 10-year probability of major osteoporotic fracture and hip fracture based on the FRAX model to support treatment decisions
map.绝经后女性骨密度 T 值处于骨量减少区间时，用 FRAX 做 10 年骨折风险分: When a postmenopausal woman's bone density T-score is in the osteopenia range, use FRAX to stratify 10-year fracture risk and decide whether drug intervention is needed.
map.长期口服糖皮质激素（如泼尼松≥5 mg/日超过 3 个月）患者的骨折风险机会性筛: Opportunistic fracture risk screening for patients on long-term oral glucocorticoids (for example prednisone ≥ 5 mg/day for more than 3 months).
map.社区骨质疏松症高危人群（低体重、跌倒史、早绝经）的筛查与补钙/维生素 D 建议制: Screening of community groups at high risk of osteoporosis (low body weight, fall history, early menopause) and formulation of calcium/vitamin D recommendations.
map.65 岁女性 FRAX 评估示例: FRAX assessment example for a 65-year-old woman
map.：输入：年龄 65、女性、BMI 24、既往脆性骨折 1 次、无父母髋骨折史、不: : Inputs: age 65, female, BMI 24, one previous fragility fracture, no parental hip fracture history, non-smoker, no glucocorticoid use, no alcohol. The tool returns the 10-year probability of major osteoporotic fracture and of hip fracture, and compares them with national intervention thresholds (for example a major fracture probability of at least 20% or hip fracture at least 3%), indicating that anti-osteoporosis treatment should be started in combination with the bone density T-score.
map.糖化白蛋白(GA)与血糖相关性评估器: Glycated albumin (GA) and glycemia correlation evaluator
map.适用于 40–90 岁、尚未接受抗骨质疏松治疗的人群；已治疗者结果会被低估。不能: Suitable for people aged 40-90 who have not yet received anti-osteoporosis treatment; results are underestimated for those already treated. It cannot replace bone density measurement and comprehensive clinical judgment.
map.FRAX 没包含跌倒因素，怎么用？: FRAX does not include fall risk factors - how should it be used?
map.FRAX 评估的是骨折内在骨强度风险，高跌倒风险者（老年、神经肌肉疾病）应结合临: FRAX assesses the intrinsic bone-strength risk of fracture; people at high fall risk (elderly, neuromuscular disease) should be assessed separately in the clinical context, and more active intervention is advisable when results are close to the threshold.
